- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 85+ values), then correct downward — model fails to fully adjust downward after peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates when history is trending down, underestimates when trending up — fails to capture momentum.
- Forecast for day 1 often too low relative to true outcome, suggesting lag in capturing recent history.
- Model underestimates the “bottom” of the price range (e.g., 75–78) when true outcome dips, especially after a spike.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values in the middle of the 30-day window, especially when history includes recent highs.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven patterns (e.g., October dips) — consistently misses downward corrections after mid-month spikes.
